v1_evidence: protocol/receiver.py:114-121 unconditionally terminated self._session on any incoming HANDSHAKE_INIT before authentication; no timestamp, nonce, rate limit, or replay cache.
v2_change: Isolated Receiver._pending_session from active Receiver._session; added timestamp freshness check (60s), 16B handshake_nonce, bounded replay cache (1024 entries), sliding-window rate limiter, and 10s pending timeout in protocol/receiver.py and protocol/messages.py.
Residual_risk: Volumetric packet flooding at the radio/link layer still requires Layer 1 spread-spectrum/rate-limiting controls.

v1_evidence: protocol/receiver.py:194 called session.complete_handshake() inside process_handshake_init(), entering ESTABLISHED before HANDSHAKE_CONFIRM was verified.
v2_change: Added SessionState.AWAITING_CONFIRM, Session.stage_handshake(), and Session.confirm_handshake() in protocol/session.py; Receiver only promotes _pending_session to _session after HANDSHAKE_CONFIRM decryption and ML-DSA-65 signature verification succeed.

v1_evidence: protocol/messages.py:216-245 set sender_kem_key=b'' in HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE and omitted recipient_id and responder nonce from the signed payload.
v2_change: Updated HandshakePayload in protocol/messages.py to include recipient_id, timestamp, and 16B handshake_nonce, and echoed initiator's 1184B sender_kem_key in HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE; verified both in Sender.process_handshake_response().

v1_evidence: protocol/sender.py:173 and protocol/receiver.py:193 concatenated raw init_packet + resp_packet without length prefixes or domain-separation label.
v2_change: Added Session.append_transcript() with 4-byte big-endian uint32 length framing over full wire packets (including 22B headers) and prepended TRANSCRIPT_CONFIRM_LABEL before ML-DSA-65 signing/verification.

v1_evidence: protocol/crypto_core.py passed keys, ciphertexts, and signatures to liboqs without pre-FFI FIPS 203/204 byte-length validation; messages did not bind algorithm identifiers.
v2_change: Enforced exact FIPS 203 (1184/2400/1088 B) and FIPS 204 (1952/4032/3309 B) byte lengths in protocol/crypto_core.py and bound kem/sig/aead/kdf algorithm strings in HandshakePayload.
Residual_risk: Internal liboqs C implementation correctness is assumed as a trusted third-party library.

v1_evidence: protocol/session.py:67-116 derived traffic keys in a single HKDF stage without binding SHA256(transcript) or peer identities (initiator_id, responder_id).
v2_change: Implemented two-stage HKDF-SHA-256 key schedule (derive_epoch_root_secret + SessionKeys.from_root_secret) binding session_id, epoch, SHA256(transcript), initiator_id, and responder_id.

v1_evidence: protocol/receiver.py only called validate_received_nonce() in _handle_command(), omitting HANDSHAKE_CONFIRM, REKEY, and TERMINATE.
v2_change: Added validate_received_nonce() to Receiver.process_handshake_confirm(), Receiver._handle_rekey(), Receiver._handle_terminate(), and Sender.complete_rekey().

v1_evidence: protocol/session.py:182-183 stored all emitted and received nonces in unbounded Python sets growing O(N) up to 2^20 entries per epoch.
v2_change: Replaced unbounded sets with a sliding-window deque + set bounded to NONCE_WINDOW_SIZE = 200 entries plus a monotonic counter cutoff.
Residual_risk: Packets delayed by more than MAX_SEQUENCE_GAP (100) or NONCE_WINDOW_SIZE (200) are dropped by design.

v1_evidence: protocol/constants.py:92-102 defined VALID_COMMANDS but neither CommandPayload nor Receiver/Sender enforced it.
v2_change: Enforced command in VALID_COMMANDS, printable ASCII checks, and field length bounds in CommandPayload.from_json_bytes() and Sender.send_command().
Residual_risk: Semantic validation of command parameters (e.g. waypoint coordinates) belongs to Layer 3 flight control logic.

v1_evidence: protocol/messages.py allowed NaN, Infinity, and negative timestamps in CommandPayload and Receiver did not check command timestamp freshness.
v2_change: Added _strict_json_loads() rejecting NaN/Infinity/-Infinity, _validate_finite_timestamp() requiring finite positive numbers, and 60s timestamp freshness enforcement in Receiver._handle_command().
Residual_risk: Requires Ground Station and UAV wall clocks to remain synchronized within +/- 60 seconds.

v1_evidence: protocol/receiver.py:293-315 executed ML-DSA-65 sig_verify (~0.51 ms) before checking sequence number replay/window bounds.
v2_change: Moved session.validate_recv_sequence(header.sequence) into Receiver.receive_packet() before dispatching or running ML-DSA-65 sig_verify.
Residual_risk: An attacker with current symmetric session keys can still force one AES-256-GCM decryption (~0.0037 ms) per fresh sequence number.

v1_evidence: protocol/sender.py:249-297 and receiver.py:322-360 performed rekey using raw unsigned KEM keys encrypted only under current session keys and did not mix previous epoch root secret.
v2_change: Introduced ML-DSA-65 signed RekeyPayload with epoch binding, 16B rekey_nonce, echoed KEM public key, 32B HMAC-SHA-256 key confirmation tag, and root-secret chaining (prev_root_secret || kem_shared_secret).

v1_evidence: protocol/sender.py:265 transitioned session to REKEYING before response validation without rollback on error; TERMINATE payload was unsigned.
v2_change: Implemented prepare_rekey(), commit_rekey(), and abort_rekey() so failed rekey responses roll back cleanly to ESTABLISHED; replaced raw TERMINATE with ML-DSA-65 signed TerminatePayload.

v1_evidence: protocol/session.py:216 used wall-clock time.time() for session lifetime expiration checks.
v2_change: Updated Session._elapsed_seconds() to use time.monotonic() while preserving compatibility with test adjustments to session.created_at.
Residual_risk: Wall-clock timestamps are still used for inter-peer message freshness (which requires loosely synchronized clocks).

v1_evidence: protocol/identity.py, sender.py, and receiver.py never checked peer roles (ground_station vs uav), allowing an authenticated UAV peer to send commands as a ground station.
v2_change: Added TrustStore.verify_peer_role() and enforced ground_station initiator and uav responder roles across Sender.initiate_handshake, Sender.process_handshake_response, Receiver.process_handshake_init, and Receiver._verify_established_sender.
Residual_risk: Fine-grained per-command RBAC across multiple ground station operators is out of scope for Layer 2.

v1_evidence: protocol/session.py:345 set key references to None without overwriting mutable byte buffers.
v2_change: Added mutable bytearray mirrors and best-effort zero-fill in SessionKeys.clear() and Session._clear_secrets(); documented CPython immutable bytes garbage-collection limitation.
Residual_risk: CPython immutable bytes objects created by cryptography/liboqs cannot be deterministically zeroed from pure Python prior to GC.

v1_evidence: protocol/identity.py:92 compared signing public keys using == instead of hmac.compare_digest.
Residual_risk: Public signing keys are non-secret values; constant-time comparison is defense-in-depth hygiene.
